title: Token-budgeted context packing tool (sutra_context)
description:
Add a new `sutra_context` tool that packs target symbol + dependencies + dependents within a token budget, with graceful degradation. Currently sutra_read caps by line count (500 lines) and sutra_explore/winnow cap by item count — no token awareness.

sem's approach: strict priority cascade — target entity > direct deps > direct dependents > transitive deps > transitive dependents. Target gets budget first with graceful degradation: full body → head-truncated (70% cap) → bare signature → omitted (target_omitted flag). Neighbors capped so no single dep can cost more than target did. Tests tallied into OmittedTail counts rather than packed as full bodies. Token estimation is heuristic (char/token ratio).

Key design decisions for sutra's version:
- Can we reuse sutra_impact's existing BFS for deps/dependents rather than reimplementing?
- sutra_read already has the symbol body retrieval — compose rather than duplicate
- sem also has an "attention ledger" (dedup repeated identical queries, return "unchanged" one-liner) — worth considering as part of this design
- Token estimation: simple char ratio vs. tiktoken/actual tokenizer tradeoff

Reference implementation:
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/parser/context.rs` — `build_context_result_bounded()`, priority packing, graceful degradation, `estimate_tokens()`
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-mcp/src/server.rs` — `sem_context` tool params (budget default 8000, hops), attention ledger (`ledger_reply`, `LedgerFill`)

Sutra infrastructure to build on:
- `sutra/src/tools/impact.rs` — existing BFS for deps/dependents
- `sutra/src/tools/read.rs` — symbol body retrieval
- `sutra/src/graph.rs` — GraphData adjacency maps

License: MIT → AGPL fine with attribution.

decisions.decision: Inline BFS walks in context.rs rather than extracting shared helper from calls.rs
decisions.rationale: calls.rs BFS is call-only, keeps unresolved refs, and emits per-ref entries; context.rs walks all edge types, deduplicates by symbol ID, and returns SymbolRows. A shared abstraction parameterized across both would be more complex than the duplicated ~40 lines.
decisions.rejected: Extract shared walk_callers/walk_callees from calls.rs and refactor both modules onto it

implementation_plan:
Design settled 2026-07-10. Reality check from exploration: impact.rs BFS is dependents-only and discards symbol ids/spans before returning (only counts, or name/file/edge_type under explain); calls.rs is bidirectional but also serializes away the SymbolRows it already resolved; sutra_read always reads disk fresh with a single hard line-cut (no degradation tiers); the only token concept anywhere is explore.rs's `lines*4` per-item estimate under a COUNT-based budget. So: new packer composing DB queries + shared helpers, not a wrapper over existing tool handlers. Attention ledger DEFERRED to sutra/253.

Plan:
1. Extract a shared neighbor-walk helper from calls.rs collect_callers/collect_callees (calls.rs:89-195) that returns SymbolRows (id + start/end lines intact) instead of serialized entries; refactor calls.rs onto it. This kills the second name-based resolve round-trip a packer would otherwise need.
2. New src/tools/context.rs — handle(db, symbol, token_budget=8000, depth=2). Priority tiers: target → direct callees → direct callers → transitive callees → transitive callers (sem's cascade).
3. Port sem's packing from /home/josh/soft/sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/parser/context.rs build_context_result_bounded (L124-288):
   - Target ladder: full body if it fits → head-truncated capped at budget*7/10 (whole lines, explicit "… truncated: N more lines" marker that must itself fit) → bare signature → target_omitted=true with early return (no neighbors if target can't fit).
   - Per-neighbor cap: max(target_tokens_used, budget/10); oversized neighbors degrade to signature-only, never silently omitted.
   - Transitive tiers signature-only, hard cap 25 per role; stub-signature filtering.
   - Tests not packed for non-test targets — tallied into omitted{role, entities, tests} counts (exception: target itself is a test).
4. estimate_tokens = max(words*13/10, chars/4) in a small shared module (sem's tuned heuristic — the words-only variant undercounted dense code 2-3x). Retrofit explore.rs's lines*4 to call it.
5. Neighbor ordering within tiers — sutra's edge over sem: EdgeKind::clustering_weight() (graph.rs:38-46, Call 1.0 > FieldAccess 0.8 > TypeUse 0.5 > Import 0.3 > Reference 0.2), then symbol pagerank. sem packs in discovery order; we rank.
6. Body retrieval: reuse/extract read.rs's file-slicing + collect_relevant_imports helpers (read.rs:124-140, 207-260). Lessons surfacing via LessonsDb::query_for_context + apply_staleness, same pattern as read.rs:176-202.
7. MCP registration per mcp.rs pattern: ContextArgs {workspace: String, symbol: String, token_budget: Option<usize>, depth: Option<usize>} with #[tool] handler, ctx.wrap envelope. Response shape mirrors sem: {symbol, file, token_budget, tokens_used, truncated, target_omitted, context[{symbol,kind,file,role,tokens,content}], omitted[{role,entities,tests}]}.

Tests: budget large enough for everything → full bodies; tight budget → target head-truncated at 70%, neighbors signature-only; budget smaller than signature → target_omitted early return; test-neighbor tallying; deterministic ordering by edge weight/pagerank.
execution_record: Implemented as planned with one deviation: did NOT extract a shared neighbor-walk helper from calls.rs (plan step 1). The behavioral differences between calls.rs (call-only BFS, per-ref entries, unresolved-name handling) and context.rs (all-edge-type BFS, deduped by symbol ID, SymbolRow-based) meant a shared abstraction would need enough parameterization to be more complex than the two separate ~40-line BFS loops. Instead, context.rs composes DB queries directly (find_refs_in_file, find_refs_to_symbol, symbol_by_id, find_enclosing_symbol) — matching the decision recorded in the task. Did not retrofit explore.rs's lines*4 estimate to use estimate_tokens (plan step 4 mention) — deferred as separate cleanup. Made collect_relevant_imports pub(crate) in read.rs to reuse for target imports.

messages.text:
Codex adversarial review: approve with notes (post-fix).

Codex found 4 real issues, all fixed in e02991b:
1. [high] Import lines could replace target signature under tight budgets — imports now separated from body for packing decisions
2. [medium] Parser-flagged tests (FLAG_TEST/FLAG_CFG_TEST) not caught by name heuristics — now checks sym.flags
3. [medium] Direct neighbors silently dropped when body unreadable + no DB signature — now tallied in omitted
4. [medium] Unbounded BFS traversal — clamped depth to 4, added 500-node walk cap

All 1233 tests pass post-fix.
